subject.title: fix(openai): bound blob websocket message reads

question: Should the provider reject Blob-like WebSocket messages using the existing 16 MiB HTTP success-body limit, or should it use a separately documented Codex WebSocket limit?
rationale: This is a user-visible compatibility boundary: the branch newly rejects some messages, while the supplied evidence does not establish that the reused HTTP cap is the upstream WebSocket contract.

options.title: Verify and retain the shared limit
options.body: Confirm the Codex/runtime protocol supports the 16 MiB bound, then remove the test-only export and land the private transport-level coverage.

options.title: Use a WebSocket-specific contract
options.body: Adopt a documented WebSocket message limit if the upstream/runtime contract differs from the HTTP success-body cap.

options.title: Pause the hardening change
options.body: Do not introduce a new rejection boundary until the protocol limit and upgrade behavior can be demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Verify and retain the shared limit
recommendation.body: Confirm the Codex/runtime protocol supports the 16 MiB bound, then remove the test-only export and land the private transport-level coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work is the closest available ownership trail for the native Codex Responses WebSocket transport.
